**Analysis of the test image:**

**Affected plant part**: Leaf (appears to be a tomato leaf)

**Key visual features observed**:
- Extensive yellowing (chlorosis) across large portions of the leaf
- Brown necrotic tissue concentrated in wedge/V-shaped areas, particularly along the left and lower portions of the leaf
- Necrosis appears to originate from certain points and extends inward from the leaf margins
- Dark browning visible along the veins in affected areas
- No discrete circular spots with concentric rings (rules out Early Blight, Target Spot, Septoria)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No water-soaked oily blotches or cottony sporulation (rules out Late Blight)
- No olive-green velvety mold (rules out Leaf Mold)

**Reasoning**:
The combination of widespread interveinal yellowing, V-shaped brown necrotic lesions extending inward from leaf margins, and prominent vascular browning along the leaf veins is a hallmark presentation of **Verticillium Wilt**. The symptom description explicitly mentions "V-shaped lesions extending inward from leaf margins" with "brown necrotic tissue" developing within those lesions — which matches precisely what is visible in this image. The systemic, non-discrete nature of the browning (not circular spots) further differentiates this from fungal leaf spot diseases.
